questions.stem: The Stanley Reservoir, popularly known as the Mettur Dam, is built across which river in Tamil Nadu?

options.option_text: Krishna River, flowing through Andhra Pradesh
Cauvery River, flowing through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
Godavari River, the widest river in peninsular India
Tapti River, emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat

questions.explanation: Mettur Dam (officially Stanley Reservoir) is built on the Cauvery River in Salem district, Tamil Nadu; completed in 1934, it was among the largest dams in India at the time. Godavari and Krishna are also major peninsular rivers but run further north and do not enter Tamil Nadu — a common geography mix-up.

questions.stem: The Koyna Dam, one of India's largest hydroelectric power stations, is situated in which state?

options.option_text: Karnataka, home to several Sahyadri hydroelectric projects
Goa, situated along the western Konkan coastal belt
Maharashtra, within the Sahyadri mountain range zone
Madhya Pradesh, on the northern edge of the Deccan plateau

questions.explanation: Koyna Dam is located on the Koyna River in Satara district, Maharashtra, and forms the backbone of Maharashtra's hydroelectric grid. Karnataka is a common distractor because the Sahyadri/Western Ghats also hosts Karnataka dams like Sharavathi, but Koyna is entirely within Maharashtra.

questions.stem: The Tehri Dam in Uttarakhand is constructed at the confluence of which two rivers?

options.option_text: Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meeting near Dev Prayag
Yamuna and Tons rivers near Kalsi in Uttarakhand
Bhagirathi and Bhilangna rivers near old Tehri town
Ganga and Mandakini meeting at Rudraprayag confluence

questions.explanation: Tehri Dam is built at the Bhagirathi–Bhilangna confluence in Tehri Garhwal district. Option A is the top distractor: Alaknanda meets Bhagirathi at Dev Prayag to form the Ganga, but that confluence is 30 km downstream of the dam site — a precise fact many candidates confuse.

questions.stem: The Srisailam Dam on the Krishna river is a joint inter-state project shared between which two Indian states?

options.option_text: Karnataka and Maharashtra, along the upper Krishna basin
Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, sharing the Krishna river
Odisha and Chhattisgarh, built across the Mahanadi river
Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, on the Wainganga river

questions.explanation: Srisailam Dam lies on the Krishna River on the Telangana–Andhra Pradesh border; both states operate separate powerhouses (Left Bank: AP; Right Bank: Telangana). Karnataka and Maharashtra are upper-riparian Krishna states and a common distractor, but they do not share the Srisailam dam site itself.

questions.stem: The Idukki Dam in Kerala is notable as India's first arch dam. What is its precise structural classification?

options.option_text: Gravity dam, which resists pressure through its own dead weight
Earthen embankment dam, built with layers of compacted soil
Double-curvature arch dam, transferring thrust to canyon walls
Rockfill dam, constructed using compacted rock and gravel fill

questions.explanation: Idukki Dam (on the Periyar River) is a double-curvature arch dam — it curves both horizontally and vertically so water pressure is transmitted to the valley walls, not the foundation alone. Completed in 1974, it was the first arch dam built in Asia. Gravity dams (option A) resist entirely by dead weight, making A the most plausible wrong choice.

questions.stem: The Baglihar Dam on the Chenab River in J&K triggered a formal dispute with Pakistan under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty. Through which mechanism was this dispute ultimately resolved?

options.option_text: Referral to the International Court of Justice at The Hague
Appointment of a Neutral Expert by the World Bank in 2005
Bilateral talks through the Permanent Indus Commission forum
Arbitration before the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague

questions.explanation: Pakistan objected to Baglihar's design and the World Bank appointed Swiss engineer Prof. Raymond Lafitte as Neutral Expert in 2005; his 2007 ruling largely upheld India's design with minor modifications. Option D (Permanent Court of Arbitration) is the trickiest distractor — that route was used later for the Kishenganga dispute, not Baglihar. These two cases are frequently confused in exams.

questions.stem: The Pong Dam (Maharana Pratap Sagar) in Himachal Pradesh, built on the Beas River, is protected under which international instrument for its importance as a migratory waterfowl habitat?

options.option_text: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) signed at Rio de Janeiro
Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance
Bonn Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) framework
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES)

questions.explanation: Pong Dam Lake was designated Ramsar Wetland Site No. 1209 in 2002; it hosts over 220 bird species including Bar-headed Goose and various migratory waterfowl. CMS (option C) governs conservation of migratory animals themselves — a plausible distractor — but it does not confer 'wetland of international importance' status, which is exclusively a Ramsar designation.
